{{Quote|I burn his armor and with it the name of Darth Vader. May the name of Anakin Skywalker be a light that guides the Jedi for generations to come&hellip; Rest well, father. The Force is with you.|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], after lighting the funeral pyre|<ref name="RadioDrama" />}}
The '''funeral of Anakin Skywalker''' took place on [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], after [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] died aboard the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] during the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. Skywalker was redeemed by his son, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]], and fulfilled the prophecy of the [[Chosen One/Legends|Chosen One]] by destroying the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], but the redemption cost Skywalker his life. Upon [[Death/Legends|death]], Skywalker's body disappeared and his soul became one with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], leaving behind only the [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|armor of Darth Vader]].

Luke escaped the Death Star with his father's armor just before the battle station was destroyed by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. Once on Endor, Luke built a [[Jedi funeral/Legends|funeral]] pyre and [[Cremation/Legends|lit]] the armor on fire, declaring his hope that the name of Anakin Skywalker would be a light to guide the [[New Jedi Order|new Jedi]]. After the funeral ended, Luke joined the Rebel and [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] victory celebration, where he saw the [[Force ghost/Legends|spirit]] of his father&mdash;along with the spirits of [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]&mdash;proudly watching the celebration.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|I'll not leave you here. I've got to save you."<br />"You already have, Luke. You were right. You were right about me. Tell your sister, you were right.|Luke and Anakin Skywalker, in the moments before Anakin's death|<ref name="ROTJ" />}}
During the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] was redeemed from the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of]] [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and once again became Anakin Skywalker. His redemption came when he chose to save his son, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], who was being [[Force lightning/Legends|electrocuted]] by [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. Anakin threw Palpatine, his [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] master, down the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star's]] reactor shaft, killing the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]].<ref name="ROTJ" /> Through this decision, Skywalker fulfilled his destiny as the [[Chosen One/Legends|Chosen One]] and brought balance to the Force through the destruction of the Sith.<ref name="ROTSDVD">{{Film|III}} DVD commentary</ref>

[[File:Anakinredeemed.png|thumb|left|300px|Anakin Skywalker in the moments before his death.]]
The choice to save Luke ended up being a sacrifice; Palpatine's lightning attack hit Anakin when the redeemed Jedi grabbed and threw his master, leading to Skywalker's life-supporting [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|suit of armor]] becoming damaged. Luke attempted to save his father by bringing him to a shuttle, but Anakin insisted that his [[Death/Legends|death]] was imminent. At his father's request, Luke removed the helmet from Skywalker's head, allowing the Chosen One to look at his son with his own eyes for the first and last time. Anakin comforted Luke, reminding his son that despite his imminent physical death, Luke had saved him in the one way that truly mattered, and died not before telling Luke that he was right about Anakin. <ref name="ROTJ" /> His body disappeared,<ref name="AnakinDatabankArchive">{{DB|character|anakinskywalker|Anakin Skywalker|oldversion=20110731185732}}</ref> and Anakin became one with the Force.<ref name="LifeLegendKenobi">''[[The Life and Legend of Obi-Wan Kenobi]]''</ref>

==The funeral==
{{Quote|&hellip;first you're going to light Lord Vader's funeral&mdash;that is your father's funeral pyre, sir?"<br />"What could be more fitting? It's a night of lights, Ewok victory fires, Rebel fireworks, even the last pieces of the Death Star burning up in the atmosphere."<br />"Put that way, Master Luke, it does sound appropriate.|C-3PO and Luke Skywalker, during the funeral|<ref name="RadioDrama" />}}
[[File:Anakinfuneral.png|thumb|right|300px|Darth Vader's armor burns on the funeral pyre.]]
With Skywalker's body gone, Luke escaped from the Death Star with the empty armor just before the station was destroyed by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. Luke brought the armor to [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], where the Alliance and the native [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] were celebrating the defeat of Palpatine and the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and constructed a funeral pyre outside of the Ewok village.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Although initially alone, he was joined by [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], who asked Luke to join the Ewok victory celebration. Luke told C-3PO he would be right along, but first [[Cremation/Legends|lit fire]] to the armor in the hopes that the mistakes of Darth Vader would be shed and that the name of Anakin Skywalker would become a light to guide the [[New Jedi Order|new Jedi]] for generations.<ref name="RadioDrama" />

==Aftermath==
After the funeral, Luke joined the Rebel celebration in the Ewok village, reuniting with his friends, as well as his twin sister [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]. As Luke stepped away from the celebration, he saw the [[Force ghost/Legends|spirits]] of his Jedi masters, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], quietly watching the evening's festivities. Anakin appeared beside them, proudly watching his son as Luke looked on, happy to see his father having become one with the Force. Luke bid them farewell and rejoined the celebration,<ref name="ROTJ" /> with the knowledge that the Jedi had returned.<ref name="RadioDrama" />

==Behind the scenes==
Anakin Skywalker's funeral is a scene from [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], taking place after Anakin's death aboard the second Death Star. When ''Return of the Jedi'' was shot, the funeral scene was originally not in the film. It was not until after the conclusion of principal photography that [[George Lucas]] and his creative team chose to insert it. Because Anakin's death scene ended with the character in Luke's arms, Lucas was concerned the audience would believe the character was not dead and that he would come back, or there would be audience confusion as to what Luke did with Anakin's body. Producer [[Howard G. Kazanjian]] was initially opposed to inserting the scene, which aimed to clarify that potential confusion, but changed his mind once he saw an animatic version of the scene.<ref name="MakingOfJedi">''[[The Making of Return of the Jedi]]''</ref>

With the decision having been made to include the funeral pyre in the film, the scene was then scripted, given a storyboard treatment by [[Joe Johnston]], and shot.<ref name="MakingOfJedi" /> The scene was filmed near [[Skywalker Ranch]] a few months before ''Return of the Jedi'' opened in theaters.

For years, ''Star Wars'' [[canon]] stated that Anakin's body was burned on the funeral pyre; ''Return of the Jedi'' does not show his body disappearing, and the [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|film novelization]] says that the body was burned.<ref name="ROTJNovel">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' film novelization]]</ref> Later, in the [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] continuity, it was established that Anakin's body disappeared after his death, and that Luke burned Darth Vader's empty armor on Endor.<ref name="AnakinDatabankArchive" />
